title: Machine travel check refuses large-radius arcs: it judges the quarter points of the full circle, not the swept arc

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

A 2D Contour around a part of about 1128 x 822 mm does not post. The machine check reports 40+ travel problems. The part, the stock and the work offset (G54) are correct.

```
post blocked - machine grblHAL 3-axis: 40 limit problem(s):
2D Contour1: move 31 reaches 21864.484 in X, the stroke is -3000.000..3000.000;
2D Contour1: move 31 reaches -21346.099 in Y, the stroke is -3000.000..3000.000;
2D Contour1: move 31 reaches -22475.758 in X, the stroke is -3000.000..3000.000;
2D Contour1: move 31 reaches -43516.220 in Y, the stroke is -3000.000..3000.000;
2D Contour1: move 32 reaches 14585.152 in X, ...
... (+284 more)
```

A larger machine does not help. The reported values grow with the arc radius, not with the part.

## Expected

The check judges the points that the arc really passes through. This program stays inside a stroke of -3000..3000, so it posts.

## Evidence

The part's long sides are gentle curves. The 2D Contour cuts them as arcs with very large radii. Values are relative to G54, read from the saved toolpath:

| Move | Radius | Sweep | Chord | Quarter point X+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 31 | 22170 mm | 0.259 deg | 100.4 mm | 21864.484 |
| 32 | 14740 mm | 0.390 deg | 100.5 mm | 14585.152 |
| 33 | 11037 mm | 0.522 deg | 100.5 mm | 10981.565 |
| 34 | 8814 mm | 0.653 deg | 100.5 mm | 8839.776 |

The quarter point X+ of move 31 is exactly the value in the refusal (21864.484).

| Extent from G54 | X | Y |
|---|---|---|
| Real cut (endpoints + quarter points inside the sweep) | -4.0 .. 1128.0 | -4.1 .. 821.5 |
| What the check uses (all four quarter points) | -22475.8 .. 21864.5 | -43516.2 .. 44333.6 |

## Cause

`crates/app/src/machine/judge.rs` `move_extremes` adds all four quarter points of the arc's full circle, also when the arc does not sweep through them. The doc comment says this is on purpose ("can only over-report"). That is harmless for small arcs. For a large-radius arc it refuses a legal program on every machine size.

The same function is used by the mill stroke check (`machine/mod.rs`) and by `plasma.rs`, `waterjet.rs`, `wire_edm.rs` and `lathe_stroke.rs`.

## Proposed fix

Add a quarter point only when the arc's sweep passes it. Use the start angle, the end angle and `arc.ccw`. A full circle keeps all four quarter points. Count a quarter point that lies on an endpoint. `crates/geometry/src/sketch_data.rs` `bounds` already does this for DXF arcs.

The sweep direction is the same `ccw` that the post writes as G2/G3. Thus the check stays exact and does not hide a violation.

## How to reproduce

1. Mount a 3-axis machine (I used grblHAL 3-axis, with the X/Y travel set to -3000..3000).
2. Import a part whose outline has long, shallow curves (here: a STEP model of 1128 x 822 mm).
3. Put G54 on the part corner and fit the stock.
4. Add a 2D Contour with an 8 mm end mill (EM-0800-4FL). Generate.
5. Post. The post is refused with the travel problems above.

I can share the project file (`.camproj`) privately.

## Related

- #2585 moves `judge.rs` to `camcraft-post`. Its output must not change, so this fix is separate. The second to land rebases.
- #1882 reads `move_extremes` for program bounds and has the same over-reach.

## Done means

- A large-radius arc with a short sweep inside the stroke does not give a travel problem.
- An arc that sweeps past a quarter point outside the stroke still gives a travel problem.
- The same arc in the other direction is judged on its own side.
- A full circle keeps all four quarter points.
- The existing stroke suites stay green (`vmc_stroke`, `machine`, `lathe_stroke`, `lathe_thread_travel`, plasma, waterjet, wire).

Suggested labels (for a maintainer): `bug`, `P3` (a legal program is refused), `effort:high` (safety floor: a travel check), `area:machine`.
